query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled thermal aging treatment can induce a nanoscale dispersion of BCC precipitates within a single-phase FCC FeCoNi-based alloy, thereby increasing the coercive field beyond the typical 100 Oe observed in untreated samples.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase FCC FeCoNi (or closely matched derivative) with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity (<100 Oe).
generation.intervention: Thermal aging treatment via controlled annealing.
generation.conditions: Annealing at approximately 500°C for 2 hours in an inert atmosphere to avoid oxidation, ensuring uniform heat treatment.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of well-dispersed nanoscale BCC precipitates within the FCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: The nanoscale BCC precipitates act as effective domain wall pinning centers. Their presence creates energy barriers that impede domain wall motion, thus increasing the coercivity of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in coercive field relative to the untreated single-phase FCC FeCoNi alloy; coercivity is expected to exceed 100 Oe while preserving a high saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: Magnetic properties (especially coercivity <100 Oe) of the as-cast or conventionally processed single-phase FCC FeCoNi (or matched derivative) alloy.
generation.boundary: Compositionally, the intervention applies to FeCoNi-based alloys with similar elemental ratios; structurally, the initial matrix should be single-phase FCC, and magnetic measurements should be conducted under comparable field and temperature conditions as the baseline.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain, and the balance between enhanced coercivity and preservation of saturation magnetization needs to be experimentally verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples with identical single-phase FCC FeCoNi compositions. Subject one set to the specified aging treatment (500°C for 2 hours in an inert atmosphere) and leave the other set untreated. Characterize the microstructure using TEM or high-resolution XRD to confirm the presence (or absence) of nanoscale BCC precipitates. Evaluate the magnetic properties (especially coercivity) using standard magnetometry.
measurements: Coercive field (Hc) via vibrating sample magnetometry or SQUID magnetometry
Microstructural analysis (TEM/XRD) for phase identification and precipitate size/distribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not show statistically significant formation of nanoscale BCC precipitates and the measured coercivity does not increase beyond 100 Oe compared to the untreated baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The present work exhibits the effects of Sn addition on the magnetic properties and microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The results show all the samples consist of a mixed structure of face-centered-cubic (FCC) phase and body-centered-cubic (BCC) phase. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix. It also shows that the Curie temperatures (Tc) of the FCC phase and the saturation magnetization (Ms) of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs increase greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The thermomagnetic curves indicate that the phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K. This work provides a new idea for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs for their potential application as soft magnets to be used at high temperatures.

In this work, the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs were prepared by vacuum arc-melt casting. Effects of Sn content on the phase constitution and magnetic properties were studied. All the samples are composed of FCC and BCC phases, whereas some unknown phases appear with the addition of Sn. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates in the BCC matrix. Moreover, the Ms increases greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases with the increasing of x for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs. The addition of Sn can obviously increase the Curie temperature of the FCC phase. The phase of alloys with a mixture of FCC and BCC will transform from FCC to BCC phase at high temperature, leading to an increase of magnetization. They can be used as new soft magnetic materials at high temperatures.
